area_02b_multi_session_source_verdict.one_operational_caveat_not_a_code_defect: soak_summary.json is OVERWRITTEN (Path.write_text, L1250), not appended, at the end of EVERY invocation, under a fixed filename with no session id. Two consequences the operations design must handle procedurally (NOT by changing collector code): (1) build_soak_summary()'s per-stream raw_bytes/raw_lines are recomputed by re-reading the ACTUAL file from disk (_count_file_bytes_and_lines(), L943-953) and are therefore CUMULATIVE across every session that has ever written to this runtime_dir, whereas message_count/written_count come from the writer object's own in-memory counters and reset to 0 at every new process start -- so after a second session, a single soak_summary.json would show cumulative raw_bytes alongside a session-2-only message_count, and its bytes_per_second/projected_gb_per_day fields (cumulative bytes divided by session-2's own actual_duration_seconds) would be MISLEADINGLY INFLATED. The operations layer must compute its own per-session and cumulative throughput from operational_sessions.jsonl + raw-file byte deltas, and must NOT read soak_summary.json's bytes_per_second/projected_gb_per_day fields as meaningful once a runtime_dir has been reused across more than one session. That configuration was frozen ONLY for the Formal Start 900-second acceptance window. Long-running collection must recognize that network reality changes during normal computer use (switching proxy nodes, turning TUN on/off, using/stopping a game accelerator such as UU, changing interface/DNS) and record each such change as an ordinary, auditable operational fact -- never silently, and never as an automatic dataset-invalidating event.

The v3 single-value session_end_type enum (including its v3 addition UNCLEAN_OPERATOR_INITIATED_EARLY_STOP) is replaced by the four-dimension model in session_end_dimensions_v5 above, for the reasons given in that section's rationale_for_dimensional_model. The underlying substance (an operator-initiated early stop under the current no-signal-handler collector is UNCLEAN, never falsely labeled CLEAN) is preserved exactly -- it is now expressed as cleanliness=UNCLEAN, termination_reason=OPERATOR_FORCED_TERMINATION, termination_initiator=OPERATOR, rather than as a single enum value.

session_end_dimensions_v5.rationale_for_dimensional_model: A single mutually-exclusive session_end_type enum cannot honestly represent a real scenario like 'the program hung, so I killed it via Task Manager' -- that is simultaneously about WHETHER a clean shutdown happened (no), WHO/WHAT ended it (the operator), WHY (a forced termination, not a crash), and WHAT WAS HAPPENING BEFORE the end (the process was hung). Forcing this into one flat value either produces a dishonest label (e.g. mislabeling it PROCESS_CRASH or NETWORK_LOSS when neither is what happened) or requires the enum to keep growing combinatorially. Splitting into four independent dimensions lets every real scenario be recorded exactly and honestly without inventing new enum values for every new combination. v6 FURTHER SIMPLIFICATION (PROJECT_OWNER + GPT, human-input removal): PROJECT_OWNER explicitly rejected adding any operator reason-entry step to normal Dataset operations -- Operations V1 must be mechanical-evidence-first and require no retrospective operator explanation. What actually matters is only two questions: (1) does mechanical evidence show the prior session ended via a completed clean-shutdown sequence? and (2) if not, does the disk evidence still allow safe reconciliation? Everything else (precisely which human or event caused the end) is optional color, never a required field, and never something the operator is asked to supply after the fact.

session_end_cleanliness.meaning: Whether mechanical evidence of a completed clean-shutdown sequence (writer drain -> backlog=0 -> continuity checkpoint -> clean session-end marker) actually exists on disk. This is a MECHANICAL fact, never inferred from operator intent alone.

termination_reason.meaning: The best-evidenced proximate cause of the session ending.

termination_initiator.meaning: Who/what is attributed as having ended the session.

preceding_condition.meaning: What state the session was observed to be in immediately before it ended -- descriptive context, not itself a cleanliness or cause determination.

session_end_dimensions_v5.compact_derived_label_optional: A short human-readable label MAY be derived from session_end_cleanliness + machine_observed_end_cause_v6 for display/logging convenience, but these two fields are the AUTHORITATIVE record.

network_changed_resume.new_session_id_required: Only if this resume is also a process resume (usually yes, since a resume implies a new process invocation).
network_changed_resume.new_segment_id_required: Only if data continuity cannot be mechanically proven across the network change -- per network_epoch_model.unexpected_change_while_running's three-way outcome (continue / new segment / PAUSE_REQUIRED), applied here to the resume moment instead of a mid-run event.
network_changed_resume.network_epoch_change: Always -- a new network_epoch_id is opened, tagged PLANNED_OPERATOR_CHANGE if the operator changed it deliberately ahead of this resume, or DETECTED_RUNTIME_CHANGE if only discovered at resume time.

mechanical_evidence_checklist_governs_re.principle: Resume/recovery decisions are keyed PRIMARILY on mechanically-observable evidence, never on any operator self-report (Operations V1 has no operator self-report field at all -- see v6 human-input removal).
checklist: persisted tail valid? (JSONL structural validity of each stream's tail)
checkpoint reconcilable? (continuity_checkpoint.json readable and consistent with the persisted tails)
process/session identity known? (can the prior session's worker identity be established via the existing nonce+CIM chain, or the checkpoint's own recorded identity)
gap/resync provenance sufficient? (can any discontinuity across the boundary be either proven absent, or properly closed as an explicit gap with resync evidence)
mechanical_evidence_checklist_governs_re.consequence: SUPERSEDED IN v6 -- see mechanical_reconciliation_checklist_v6 above. session_end_cleanliness=CLEAN with a verified clean marker routes to planned_clean_resume (PROJECT_OWNER alone). ANY OTHER cleanliness value (UNCLEAN, UNKNOWN, or a claimed CLEAN marker that fails verification) routes through the mechanical_reconciliation_checklist_v6: if every item PASSES, PROJECT_OWNER alone may authorize resume; GPT escalation is triggered ONLY by a FAILED or ambiguous/integrity-critical checklist result, not by the UNCLEAN/UNKNOWN status itself.

mechanical_reconciliation_checklist_v6.applies_to: Every resume where the prior session's session_end_cleanliness is UNCLEAN or UNKNOWN.
checklist: Dataset/session identity -- can the prior session and its binding to this Dataset be established?
JSONL tail validity -- is the tail of every persisted stream structurally valid (parseable, not truncated mid-record)?
last checkpoint -- is continuity_checkpoint.json present, readable, and internally consistent?
writer state -- do the writer/backlog indicators show no unresolved evidence-loss condition?
gap boundaries -- can any discontinuity across the interruption be either proven absent, or properly closed as an explicit gap with resync evidence?
required REST resync -- where a gap exists, has the required REST resync (depth snapshot / aggTrade backfill) been completed and verified?
schema/source binding -- does the resumed session bind to the same frozen schema/source scope as the Dataset (no silent schema drift)?
no concurrent collector owner -- is there no other live process already holding ownership of this runtime root (ties into EXECUTION_BLOCKER-1)?
mechanical_reconciliation_checklist_v6.outcome_all_pass: Same Dataset ID may continue. A new collection_session_id is always assigned. A new segment_id is assigned wherever continuity cannot be proven to span the interruption. PROJECT_OWNER ALONE may authorize the resume -- no GPT escalation required merely because the prior end was UNCLEAN or UNKNOWN.
mechanical_reconciliation_checklist_v6.outcome_any_fail_or_ambiguous: STOP. Escalate to PROJECT_OWNER + GPT adjudication. This is the ONLY trigger for GPT-level escalation on an ordinary interruption -- escalation is triggered by a FAILED or ambiguous/integrity-critical reconciliation result, never merely by the fact that the prior session ended UNCLEAN or UNKNOWN.
mechanical_reconciliation_checklist_v6.explicit_consequence: Ordinary power outage, ordinary reboot, Task Manager termination, a hung process force-killed, and a long machine-off period are NOT automatically GPT-escalation events and do NOT automatically invalidate the Dataset -- they route through this same bounded mechanical checklist like any other UNCLEAN/UNKNOWN case, and resume under PROJECT_OWNER's own authorization once the checklist passes.

reasons: no single-instance lock/PID ownership mechanism in the collector -- two accidental concurrent invocations against the same runtime root would both append, with no fail-closed refusal, risking duplicate collection and checkpoint/summary races

no operator-triggered graceful pause/stop path -- the only code path reaching the drain/checkpoint/summary sequence is --duration-seconds elapsing naturally (see area_02b v3 finding); an operator cannot request a clean stop mid-run today
continuous_collection_operations_readine.what_already_works_despite_this: Sequential, non-overlapping, externally-single-instance-guaranteed bounded sessions ARE already safe to append to the same Dataset/runtime root today (per the corrected verdict above). What is NOT yet safe is UNATTENDED or casually-operated continuous collection where overlap or ad-hoc early stop could occur without a safety net.
continuous_collection_operations_readine.PROJECT_OWNER_GPT_note: These two facts are NOT blockers to freezing this DESIGN_GOVERNANCE_ONLY stage -- the design itself is sound and may be finalized and written to disk. They ARE blockers to authorizing an actual continuous-collection EXECUTION phase.

execution_blockers.risk_if_unaddressed: Without single-instance enforcement, two Collector processes could be started against the same runtime root (e.g. by operator mistake, or a stale supervisor script re-launching one). Writers are not cross-process-locked, so this could cause duplicate/interleaved raw records, continuity-checkpoint write races, and soak_summary.json overwrite races -- none of which the current append-only design was built to arbitrate between two live writers.
